note: Read 2026-10-31. Majority is each province's and territory's own law; no federal Act sets one, so the country's majority is null and each is held in 'regions' from its own Act. Eighteen: Alberta, Age of Majority Act, RSA 2000, c. A-6, s. 1 (King's Printer PDF, a consolidation current as of 1 January 2002); Manitoba, The Age of Majority Act, C.C.S.M. c. A7, s. 1 (Manitoba Laws PDF). Nineteen: British Columbia, Age of Majority Act, RSBC 1996, c. 7, s. 1 (current to 27 October 2026); New Brunswick, Age of Majority Act (laws.gnb.ca, A-4), s. 1; Newfoundland and Labrador, Age of Majority Act, SNL 1995 c. A-4.2, s. 2; Nova Scotia, Age of Majority Act, RSNS 1989, c. 4, s. 2. Null, not read (the blocker file names each attempt): Ontario (e-Laws gave no text to a plain request), Quebec (LégisQuébec answered 403), Saskatchewan (no answer), Prince Edward Island (403), Yukon and Nunavut (Cloudflare challenge; Yukon's archive.org snapshot holds the same challenge page), the Northwest Territories (504 twice; its archive.org snapshot couldn't be fetched). Work: null. Employment standards are provincial and territorial (ages and performer permits differ, Ontario and British Columbia among others licensing child performers); the Canada Labour Code (s. 179, seventeen) covers only federally regulated work. The form holds no regional work rule; none was read. Service: Service is held null: no source saying no service is asked was reached today (the blocker file names the attempts); a reading only, not held: Canada has no conscription (the Canadian Armed Forces recruit volunteers).

sources.title: Age of Majority Act, RSA 2000, c. A-6 (Alberta King's Printer, current as of January 1, 2002)

sources.title: Age of Majority Act, RSBC 1996, c. 7 (BC Laws, King's Printer, current to October 27, 2026)

sources.title: Age of Majority Act, chapter A-4 (Government of New Brunswick, laws.gnb.ca)
sources.said: A person attains the age of majority and ceases to be a minor on attaining the age of nineteen years.

sources.title: Age of Majority Act, SNL 1995 c. A-4.2 (House of Assembly of Newfoundland and Labrador)
sources.said: Every person who attains the age of 19 years ... attains the age of majority; and

sources.title: Age of Majority Act, RSNS 1989, c. 4 (Nova Scotia House of Assembly)
sources.said: Every person attains the age of majority, and ceases to be a minor, on attaining ... the age of nineteen years.

sources.title: The Age of Majority Act, C.C.S.M. c. A7 (Manitoba Laws, PDF)
